title: Jason Kelce reacts to Eagles bringing back a franchise legend: ‘That’s my guy’
description: Jason Kelce weighed in on the Eagles signing Zach Ertz during ESPN's "Monday Night Football" pregame show.
fullText:
Jason Kelce and Zach Ertz helped the Philadelphia Eagles win their first Super Bowl. They played together for nearly a decade. They're both franchise legends.

So it wasn't a surprise to hear that Kelce is excited that Ertz is re-joining the Eagles.

ESPN insider Adam Schefter broke the news that Ertz is signing with the Eagles during the network's "Monday Night Football" pregame show.

Ertz's return to Philadelphia comes on the heels of Dallas Goedert's unfortunate injury news. Goedert is slated to miss a few weeks with a sprained MCL suffered in Sunday's win against the Tennessee Titans.

For Monday night's Week 3 matchup between the Eagles and the Bears, the over/under is listed at 41.5 total points on Kalshi. Our comprehensive Kalshi review makes it easy to figure out how to use their platform.

Without Goedert and with rookie Eli Stowers on IR, the Eagles had to do something to address their tight end depth.

So, they signed Ertz, the 35-year-old free agent who spent the eight-and-a-half seasons with the Eagles from 2013-21.

What were Kelce's thoughts on the move?

"Dallas has been having a heck of a year. Really upset that he's down, to be honest with you. He's been great for the offense," Kelce said on ESPN. "But listen, you don't have to talk me into Zach Ertz. That's my guy. I've got a lot of good memories with Zach. We had a lot of success. He's entrenched in Philadelphia still."

Kelce then said he "wouldn't mind seeing" Ertz make franchise history in his return.

Ertz is 11 catches away from breaking Harold Carmichael's franchise receptions record, which stands at 589.

Ertz could start chipping away at that record as early as Monday night when the Eagles face the Bears in Week 3.

Ertz will start off on the practice squad. But NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported that Ertz is expected to be elevated to the 53-man roster for next week's matchup in Chicago.

title: Steelers sign former Giants wide receiver
description: Steelers sign pair of veteran players.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are signing former New York Giants wide receiver Isaiah Hodgins to the practice squad, the team announced Tuesday. Additionally, Pittsburgh is signing cornerback Darius Rush to the practice squad.

Hodgins has been on several rosters, but most notably had his best season in 2022 with the New York Giants as they were a surprise playoff team under then-head coach Brian Daboll. Hodgins caught 33 passes and four touchdowns for the Giants that season. Last year in seven games for the Giants, he caught 10 passes and one touchdown. He also spent a brief period in Pittsburgh in 2025.

Rush is a familiar face to the Steelers, as well. He appeared in five games for Pittsburgh across the 2023 and 2024 seasons. He was a fifth-round pick of the Indianapolis Colts in the 2023 NFL Draft.

title: Patriots place G Mike Onwenu on injured reserve
description: The Patriots moved right guard Mike Onwenu to their injured reserve list on Tuesday.
fullText:
The Patriots moved right guard Mike Onwenu to their injured reserve list on Tuesday.

Onwenu left Sunday's win over the Steelers after hurting his ankle and a report later in the day said that it was broken. Head coach Mike Vrabel did not confirm that at a Monday press conference, but said Onwenu will not "be available here in the short term."

Greg Van Roten replaced Onwenu against the Steelers, but Vrabel did not rule out moving first-round pick Caleb Lomu from tackle or making other moves to replace Onwenu in the lineup.

The Patriots filled the open roster spot by signing punter Mitch Wishnowsky off of their practice squad. He was elevated for each of New England's first two games.

Tight end Tanner Conner was signed to the practice squad to round out the day's moves.

title: Tennessee will host Ohio State five-star commit for Texas game
description: Defensive line prospects in the class of 2027 and 2028 will visit Tennessee for its football game against Texas.
fullText:
2027 five-star defensive end DJ Jacobs and 2028 four-star defensive lineman Dawson Jacobs will visit Tennessee for the Vols' football game against No. 1 Texas on Saturday, according to Steve Wiltfong of Rivals.

The brothers are from Blessed Trinity Catholic High School in Roswell, Georgia. They are sons of former Georgia defensive lineman David Jacobs, who was coached by Tennessee defensive line coach Rodney Garner.

247Sports ranks DJ Jacobs as the No. 1 player in 2027 and Dawson Jacobs as the 2028 No. 15 defensive lineman and No. 15 player in Georgia.

DJ Jacobs visited Tennessee for one game during the last three seasons. He committed to Ohio State on Dec. 29, 2025. The Vols offered Dawson Jacobs a scholarship during a visit for the 2024 Tennessee-Alabama game.

West Virginia was the first school to offer Dawson Jacobs a scholarship on Oct. 1, 2024. Other schools to offer him scholarships include Florida, Florida State, Kentucky, South Carolina, USC, Central Michigan, Texas A&M, Texas, Purdue, LSU, Georgia Tech, Miami, Nebraska, SMU, Georgia, Oklahoma, Auburn, Oregon, Arkansas, Kansas, Alabama, Ohio State, Notre Dame, Ole Miss, Virginia Tech, Vanderbilt, Clemson and UCLA.

Quarterback Kaden Craft is Tennesse's only 2028 commitment.

title: U.S. Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker wanted J.J. Spaun to make him 'look like an idiot'
description: There were no points up for grabs Tuesday at the Presidents Cup but U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker claimed what felt like a 'W' in his first press conference of the week.
fullText:
MEDINAH, Ill. – There were no points up for grabs Tuesday at the Presidents Cup but U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker claimed what felt like a 'W' in his first press conference of the week.

About halfway through Snedeker's press conference, he was asked about J.J. Spaun's comments on Sunday following his victory at the BMW PGA Championship on the DP World Tour.

"I played with a huge chip on my shoulder. I definitely had something to prove this week, but everything happens for a reason," Spaun said. "The extra motivation, I think that is the willpower that you have. Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple weeks ago was very disappointing and I wanted to prove that I deserve to be on that team."

Snedeker could have defended his decision to skip Spaun, who was ranked 16th in the world and was 10th on the U.S. points list, but said Sunday's victory was an example of how top players are motivated.

"First of all, I'm super excited for J.J. What he did at Wentworth was impressive coming down the stretch," Snedeker said. "That being said, he's a competitor. Like I knew this was going to happen. I told all the guys that didn't make the team, like your job is to go make me look like an idiot as quick as possible."

Spaun said his conversation with Snedeker regarding his captain's picks was "like a 45-second phone call" and that the captain told him he was the "odd man out."

Snedeker, however, said he was comfortable with his six picks – including Patrick Cantlay, Chris Gotterup, Jackson Koivun, Xander Schauffele, Justin Thomas and Jacob Bridgeman, who also won on Sunday at the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship.

"The best advice I got from all the captains I talked to and even coaches, you've got to trust your gut. My gut was telling me one thing," Snedeker said. "You've got to make those decisions. It's tough. I feel awful for J.J., and I always will, because he's a great dude and I love the guy to death."

Medinah's test: Early OB threat, drivable 12th, not firm enough?

Medinah's No. 3, redesigned by International captain Geoff Ogilvy, will feature an alternate routing for this week's Presidents Cup, which puts OB firmly in play on the first few holes, shifts the drivable 16th earlier in the order, and might not play as firm as desired.

title: No rest (yet?) for the regulars in first Braves game after clinch
description: Whadda ya mean, they clinched the division?!
fullText:
Did you think there were going to be days off? There are no days off. At least not yet. Maybe a partial day off? We'll see.

Last homestand of the season! #BravesCountry pic.twitter.com/LDwoOkXMeR

This is the same lineup the Braves rolled out when they last had to face a lefty (8-4 loss to the Cubs). They also used this lineup in the opener against the Cubs, which they also lost. So, maybe that fortune changes here.

The Braves have a combined four, count 'em, four PAs against Brandon Williamson. Two are from Ha-Seong Kim (strikeout, flyout), and one each comes from Michael Harris II (a homer), and Matt Olson (a homer). Kind of bizarre that the two lefties are 1-for-1 with a homer off a southpaw but… four PAs, y'all.

The Reds' lineup is at least moderately interesting, or as much as can be for a bad team playing out the string.

First of three against the Braves. 

Promoted pseudo-prospect Carlos Jorge, he of the 27 career PAs and a terrible line in them, starts at leadoff. He's joined in the outfield by another promoted prospect, Hector Rodriguez, who also hasn't hit at all but has had some more exposure.

The Reds' quartet from two through five in the lineup has hit well this season. Everyone else has hit terribly. That's not too different from how the Braves have gone through the season, though. Still, JR Ritchie has a tough test and should hopefully find it easier to loop through the rest of the lineup.

title: Steelers Bring Back Big-Bodied Cornerback
description: The Pittsburgh Steelers have re-signed cornerback Darius Rush to their practice squad, the team announced on Tuesday. Rush, 26, spent parts of […]
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have re-signed cornerback Darius Rush to their practice squad, the team announced on Tuesday.

Rush, 26, spent parts of the 2023 and 2024 seasons with the Steelers. He was released from the practice squad of the Washington Commanders last week.

The Steelers have been playing without No. 1 cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who aggravated his back injury in practice last week, and still has not reached a resolution on his contract dispute with the team. Doneiko Slaughter has been called up from the practice squad for the first two games of the 2026 season, and the Steelers can only call him up one more time this year.

A 6-foot-2 South Carolina alum, Rush first joined the Steelers when they signed him from the Kansas City Chiefs practice squad in the middle of the 2023 season. He played three games for the Steelers in 2023 and four more in 2024, playing 39 snaps of defense and 39 snaps of special teams.

"What I have on special teams is really going out there and showcasing what I can do, whether it's the gunner squad, jammer squad, kick-off, kick-off return, being a front line guy or anything like that, you know. So just to go out there and that's another way to carve my name in this organization," Rush said in 2024.

Rush was waived by the Steelers on Oct. 1, 2024, having lost his starting punt gunner job to James Pierre. Rush then re-signed with the Chiefs practice squad, where he finished the season without playing in another game.

He was waived by the Chiefs with an injury designation on Aug. 1 of last year. He signed with the Cleveland Browns on Aug. 11, 2025 but was waived in late August. He then joined the Commanders practice squad and signed a reserve/future contract with the team in January.

Rush began his professional career as a fifth-round pick by the Indianapolis Colts in the 2023 NFL Draft, but he was cut coming out of training camp. He was then claimed off waivers by the Chiefs, released by Kansas City and added to the practice squad, where Pittsburgh plucked him away.

A native of Kingstree, South Carolina, Rush played college football at the University of South Carolina, where he racked up 75 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble, 15 passes defensed and three interceptions from 2019-22.

title: GGFN Editorial | Who owns German football’s fan culture in the ‘Age of the Influencer?’
description: German football supporters have spent decades complaining about the commercialization of their sport. A newer question is now beginning to intrude on the terraces. What happens when supporters themsel...
fullText:
German football supporters have spent decades complaining about the commercialization of their sport. A newer question is now beginning to intrude on the terraces. What happens when supporters themselves become the product? The growing presence of influencers, vloggers and other content creators inside German football grounds has triggered increasingly vocal resistance from organized fan scenes.

Karlsruher SC says the subject of stadium vloggers and influencers has attracted increasing attention in recent years and that the club is already discussing the issue with the Bundesliga and other clubs. It touches media rights, privacy, commercialization, supporter culture and a deceptively difficult question: who actually gets to determine what constitutes acceptable behavior inside a football stadium?

At Dynamo Dresden, months of discussions between club and fan representatives culminated in formal restrictions on commercial stadium vlogging. In Karlsruhe, the officially recognized Supporters Karlsruhe fan umbrella organization has issued an emphatic rejection of what it calls "Fanszenen-Influencer" and stadium vloggers.

Dresden has converted concerns surrounding commercial filming into club policy while explicitly reserving enforcement for the club and its security personnel. In Karlsruhe, meanwhile, the Supporters have declared what they consider culturally unacceptable and, according to their own account, have already removed at least one influencer from the stadium.

That distinction goes directly to the heart of the wider German debate.

The Supporters Karlsruhe issued a particularly forceful statement on September 9. Their opening argument placed stadium influencers within a much broader criticism of the creator economy.

"Social media and influencers have now made their way into practically every conceivable part of everyday life," the organization wrote in an Instagram statement. "Whether fitness, cooking, travel or lifestyle, the formula is always the same: as long as the clicks are there, the reach increases and the bank account fills through crude advertising and sponsorship deals."

"By now, however, content creators are also profiting from our fan culture for their own personal gain," the statement continues. "Shirts are rated for the sake of it and fan chants are judged as though they were goods on a bargain table."

The central grievance is easy enough to understand. Active supporter groups invest enormous amounts of unpaid time and money into banners, choreographies, flags, songs and displays. Those images subsequently become some of the most recognizable visual material associated with German football. The Supporters were particularly dismissive of creators who subsequently pass judgment on those performances.

"Others set themselves up as supposed experts and judge the performances of the terrace without having even the slightest idea how much work goes into organizing a choreography or how a supporters' end actually functions," the statement notes. "At the same time, these people adorn themselves with the values, romance and imagery of our terraces in order to give themselves an authentic image."

"Those same values are trampled underfoot without hesitation as soon as the first commercial deal or additional reach is at stake," the statement concludes. "Fan culture is not a lifestyle product, a photo opportunity or a tool for your self-promotion! We do not want fan-scene influencers or stadium vloggers — neither online and certainly not here with us in the Wildpark!"

The Karlsruhe dispute escalated because the Supporters' statement also indicated that this was no longer merely rhetorical.

According to the Supporters, at least one influencer has already been removed from the stadium by members of the fan scene.

"Things become completely bizarre when they are thrown out of the stadium by the fan scene and subsequently portray themselves on social media as the great victim," the statement notes.

The claim raises an obvious question of authority. BNN notes that KSC itself holds the Hausrecht, or authority to control access and conduct inside the Wildpark, meaning the formal responsibility for removing spectators lies with the club and its stewards. KSC did not directly address the alleged ejection when asked. Instead, the club said it remained in close contact with its fan representatives and was actively mediating between them and known influencers and stadium vloggers in pursuit of a "solution-oriented dialogue."

KSC is hardly defending unrestricted commercial filming. Its existing rules already prohibit unauthorized commercial use of image, audio and video recordings inside the Wildpark. The club has also emphasized that commercial stadium recordings require permission and that existing Bundesliga media regulations already govern such content.

The Supporters' position also carries institutional weight. KSC recognizes Supporters Karlsruhe as the official umbrella organization representing fan interests and incorporates the body into its three-pillar fan-work structure.

The Supporters are entitled to articulate what they believe their fan culture should look like. They can ask visitors to respect the norms of an active terrace. They can object when choreographies or supporter work are appropriated for commercial content.

That does not automatically confer the right to enforce those cultural preferences against everybody else inside the ground. That line becomes even clearer when looking east toward Dresden.

Dynamo Dresden's stance did not appear overnight. The issue was discussed repeatedly at the club's regular Turnustreffen, structured meetings bringing together club officials, Ultras Dynamo, the Fanprojekt, supporter organizations and other fan representatives.

Yet the actual policy announced by Dresden is considerably more nuanced than the slogan suggests. Dynamo did not ban supporters from taking photographs or short personal videos. The club drew its line around commercial exploitation.

Filming match action and stadium visits with the intention of monetizing the resulting content is prohibited under the stadium rules. Dynamo explicitly grounded the restriction in protection of its own media rights and those of broadcasting partners while also citing the interests of spectators who do not want permanent cameras operating around them.

The club has since incorporated the policy into normal matchday communication. Supporters attending home matches are reminded that commercial vlogging is prohibited and instructed to contact security personnel if they believe the rule is being breached. Most importantly, Dynamo made another point explicit. Enforcement of the stadium regulations belongs exclusively to the club and the deployed security service.

Independent measures by third parties are not envisaged. Dynamo subsequently reinforced that distinction in its general season information, telling supporters to report violations to stewards while explicitly rejecting "self-justice".

That provision is particularly relevant in light of the Karlsruhe dispute. Dresden's organized fan scene participated in creating the policy. It does not possess independent authority to enforce it.

Dynamo may be the most prominent German professional club thus far to formalize its response so publicly, and Karlsruhe currently provides the most visible clash between organized supporters and creators. But the forces producing the conflict exist throughout German football. KSC itself has stressed that stadium vlogs and influencers have become increasingly prominent and that the club is exchanging views with the Bundesliga and other clubs.

The underlying legal and commercial framework is broader still. At DFB events, ticket conditions already distinguish private, non-commercial recordings from commercial exploitation and public distribution. Commercial use requires prior written approval, while unauthorized distribution of match-related video or audio can be prohibited or removed.

Professional football's media ecosystem is also increasingly structured around tightly controlled digital content. DFL media regulations specifically provide for club social-media production around Bundesliga matchdays, illustrating how carefully material created inside professional stadiums is organized and rights-managed.

At the same time, football authorities themselves increasingly work with creators. In the Frauen-Bundesliga, for example, DFB commercial regulations explicitly provide for accredited influencers and content creators to receive controlled access for certain promotional activities.

That apparent contradiction is important. German football is not rejecting the creator economy. It is actively participating in it. The dispute concerns who controls that participation. An accredited creator invited by a club, league or commercial partner is operating inside an agreed rights structure. A supporter independently monetizing footage from the terrace may not be.

For organized fan scenes, however, the question goes beyond copyright or broadcasting rights. Their concern is that clubs and leagues may be able to license commercial content involving a culture that the institutions themselves did not create. That is where the legal argument and the cultural argument begin to diverge.

There is a legitimate privacy argument here that extends well beyond ultras wishing to control images of their choreography. Many ordinary spectators simply do not want to spend 90 minutes beside somebody narrating constantly into a camera. Others may reasonably object to appearing repeatedly in footage uploaded to a large social-media audience, particularly where the creator profits from it.

A legal analysis of Dynamo's approach noted that commercial stadium videos can implicate not only clubs' media and exploitation rights but also the image and privacy rights of individual spectators. The same analysis also highlighted an obvious enforcement problem: while somebody is filming, it may not be immediately apparent whether the footage is intended as a private memory or for later commercial publication.

That makes broad declarations considerably easier than practical enforcement. Most spectators carry smartphones. Many post photographs or clips. Some maintain football accounts with a few hundred followers. Others possess audiences numbering in the hundreds of thousands. Some monetize videos directly through advertising. Others derive indirect commercial benefit from reach, sponsorships or personal branding.

Still others may film vlogs as a non-commercialized hobby. Where precisely does the supporter end and the influencer begin? The line cannot realistically be determined by whether somebody holds a phone in the air. Dresden has therefore chosen a more workable distinction: private documentation remains permissible; commercial exploitation requires authorization.

The strongest part of the organized-supporter criticism concerns appropriation. If a creator treats the terrace purely as set decoration, monetizes a choreography produced through somebody else's labor and leaves again with little interest in the community responsible for it, the active scene has an understandable reason to object.

The weaker version of the argument is that documenting football for an online audience is inherently incompatible with authentic support. Football itself plainly no longer operates on that assumption.

Content creators form part of the Bundesliga's wider media environment. League and association campaigns use influencers to reach younger and more digitally oriented audiences. Clubs maintain their own social-media departments and increasingly produce matchday material specifically for mobile platforms.

The creator is therefore not automatically an intruder simply because the medium is YouTube, TikTok or Instagram. Some are supporters themselves. Some document away trips, stadium architecture, food, atmosphere or rituals for people who may never otherwise experience them. Some viewers are disabled, live abroad, cannot obtain tickets or simply want to see what a German football matchday looks like beyond the television broadcast.

Local reaction to the Karlsruhe controversy reflects precisely that split. Some supporters have backed the attempt to protect traditional terrace culture, while others question whether an organized fan body should determine who counts as a legitimate supporter. That debate will almost certainly surface elsewhere because the underlying tension exists everywhere.

The clubs market atmosphere. The leagues market atmosphere. Broadcasters market atmosphere. Supporters create much of that atmosphere. Creators increasingly want to package it for their own audiences as well. The unresolved question is how much of that culture anybody is entitled to commercialize.

Dynamo's approach potentially offers the clearer practical distinction. Private memories remain private. Commercial content requires permission. People sharing a terrace are expected to respect one another. And the club — rather than self-appointed enforcers in the stands — decides when its rules have been violated.

KSC's existing regulations already restrict commercial media use, while the club is attempting to mediate between organized supporters and creators rather than simply adopting the Supporters' declaration as stadium policy.

That is probably appropriate. Organized fan scenes possess genuine cultural authority because much of the atmosphere German football so enthusiastically markets would not exist without them.

The labor behind choreographies is real. The resentment generated when somebody else monetizes that work is understandable. So too is the desire of spectators to enjoy football without becoming unwilling extras in somebody else's content.

But cultural authority should not automatically become jurisdiction over everybody else in the stadium. The creator economy presents German football with an awkward new form of commercialization. Traditionally, supporters could direct their anger upward at broadcasters, sponsors, leagues and clubs monetizing the sport. Now individuals standing alongside them can monetize the same environment too.

Karlsruhe and Dresden happen to be where the argument has become especially visible.

They are unlikely to be where it ends.

German fan culture should not become somebody else's free film set.

Neither should the terraces become territory in which organized supporters alone determine who qualifies as a legitimate fan.

title: Penix excited in his return as Falcons starting QB
description: Michael Penix Jr. said Tuesday he finally began feeling healthy enough to play in a game late last week and had his rising confidence confirmed when his surgically repaired left knee reacted well to a strenuous workout on Saturday.  The Falcons announced on Monday that Penix will start on Thursday night at Green Bay.  The decision came one day after Cooper Rush again struggled as the fill-in starter in Sunday's 34-3 loss to NFC South rival Carolina.
fullText:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. (AP) — Michael Penix Jr. said Tuesday he finally began feeling healthy enough to play in a game late last week and had his rising confidence confirmed when his surgically repaired left knee reacted well to a strenuous workout on Saturday.

The Falcons announced on Monday that Penix will start on Thursday night at Green Bay. The decision came one day after Cooper Rush again struggled as the fill-in starter in Sunday's 34-3 loss to NFC South rival Carolina.

"I'm very excited, you know, obviously excited to be able to be out there," Penix said following Tuesday's practice. "You know, I'm going to war with my brothers, so it's very exciting when you make the final decision."

When asked if he had been targeting the Week 3 game at Green Bay, Penix said "being healthy" was his only target.

Penix said he had still been experiencing some soreness in the knee until last week. He said he spoke with coach Kevin Stefanski on Saturday. The conversation followed what Penix described as "a big workout" after he had been ruled out of the game against Carolina.

Penix said Saturday's workout was designed "just to see how my knee reacted from a big workout and it was good. So that's really kind of what helped me with that decision, my workout on Saturday, and just pushing to the limit and seeing what I can take."

Penix said when he felt no soreness on Sunday, he spoke with Stefanski to talk about how his knee had felt better through the week. Penix said he decided then he would be ready to play against the Packers but spoke with Stefanski again on Monday "just to obviously solidify that."

Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees said Tuesday that Penix has "looked sharp without any limitations" in practice. "He's moved in the pocket. He's gotten outside of the pocket."

The Falcons were 3-6 in Penix's nine starts last season. He completed 60.1% of his passes for 1,982 yards with nine touchdowns and three interceptions. Rush and rookie Jack Strand have combined to throw five interceptions with only one touchdown in two games.

Penix, Tua Tagovailoa, Rush and Strand practiced on Tuesday. Tagovailoa missed the first two games after suffering an oblique injury before Atlanta's 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers to open the season. The Falcons (0-2) have not announced who will be Penix's backup at Green Bay.

Rush struggled with accuracy and arm strength against Carolina. Rees said arm strength shouldn't be an issue for the left-handed Penix. The Falcons are looking to better utilize wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts, who have a combined seven receptions through two games.

"There's not a ton of guys out there with that arm talent," said Rees of Penix.

Penix will be making his first start since a 30-27 overtime loss to Carolina on Nov. 16, 2025. Penix tore the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee in the third quarter. He previously had two ACL injuries to his right knee and was determined to make sure he was fully recovered before returning this season.

"Whenever I felt like I can go out there, like I said, get out of all that soreness and get stronger each and every day, that's what it was always about," Penix said. "So once I felt healthy, it felt like I was ready to go."

NOTES: Cornerback A.J. Terrell will miss at least four games after being placed on injured reserve with a groin injury. Terrell suffered the injury in the first quarter against Carolina. C.J. Henderson played behind Terrell and is the probable starter at Green Bay. Terrell will be eligible to return in Week 7 against San Francisco. Defensive lineman Zach Harrison was signed to the active roster in a corresponding move. Center James Brockermeyer was released from the practice squad and offensive lineman Colby Sorsdal was signed to the practice squad.

title: Mets hiring Andy Green as full-time manager
description: Andy Green will manage the Mets in 2027, the team announced Tuesday. The interim tag he inherited when he took over for Carlos Mendoza earlier this year is gone.
fullText:
Andy Green will manage the Mets in 2027, the team announced Tuesday. The interim tag he inherited when he took over for Carlos Mendoza earlier this year is gone, with Green signing a three-year deal.

The deal represents a pivot for Green and the organization, the former because he initially said he was reluctant to manage beyond this year since it would keep him away from his family, the latter because Steve Cohen and David Stearns said they planned to conduct a search for their next manager after this season.

But people in the organization, who were careful to speak anonymously so as not to complicate his decision, said they started sensing a change in Green's mindset in recent weeks. They speculated that as a once turbulent Mets clubhouse seemed to coalesce around him, Green started warming to the possibility of balancing a dream job and his desire to by present for his daughters' final year of high school.

In fact, multiple people pointed out that there might be no better time for a father of seniors in high school to take a job like this: Given that a lockout is a near certainty and a shortened spring training – if not a delayed start to the season – seems likely enough to plan around, he might never encounter a baseball spring that would let him stay home longer.

Still, exactly what changed and when is still unclear, though as of earlier this month, Green had not approached Cohen or Stearns about any change in plans, according to people familiar with the situation.

But by Saturday's celebration of Carlos Beltran – when Beltran all but declared he was not interested in a managerial job for which he seemed like an early favorite – Green's path seemed to have cleared. The Mets decided not to subject him to the rigors of a public search before committing.

Green, 49, managed the Padres to a 274-366 record over four years from 2016-2019. He was serving as the Mets senior vice president of baseball development when they approached him about taking over for Mendoza in June.

He said then that he took the job with the understanding it would be temporary out of a sense of responsibility to the organization. He, Stearns, and Cohen maintained that approach in the months that followed, though none of them fully ruled out the possibility that something could change any one of their minds.

And while the Mets did not exactly catch fire under Green – they were 37-38 under his watch at the time of the announcement – they did seem to find a more sustainable sense of self. Carson Benge flourished. Green challenged the young starting pitchers around whom the Mets must build next year. A surprisingly effective bullpen grew from the ashes of the one the Mets dismantled at the trade deadline. Bo Bichette seemed to find new comfort and spoke glowingly of Green's people skills. Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor, well, spent the last month or two acting like two superstars working toward shared goals on perfectly good terms.

"I have a lot of respect for Andy. I think he's been good at the role that he's got right now. Not necessarily the role of managing, because I didn't see his role this year as to manage. His role, right now, was to come in and bring light, bring ownership, bring respect, and bring accountability. He's succeeded at it," Lindor told SNY last Saturday, at which point he said he had had not spoken to Green about changing his mind.

"In-game stuff, plays and all that stuff? He's made good moves, but I don't judge him on those things. I don't really care about that. He was put in here more to bring light to the players, to bring accountability, to bring respect, to bring self-awareness. And that's what he brought into the role he's in right now."

That role, of course, has been molded by the fact that the Mets have been effectively, if not mathematically, out of contention since he took over. The Padres teams he managed never played under the kind of scrutiny or expectations these Mets will next year.

But Green has passed the tests he has encountered with grace, particularly with his style of communication. His news conferences have blended candor with empathy in ways that are so far landing with both players and the public.

Last week, for example, Green navigated the emotional hurricane that was Pete Alonso's return to Citi Field without discounting his players' frustration with fans nor scolding fans for theirs. Presented with a fan base that operates with sometimes unparalleled, but often unregulated, passion, many Mets managers before him have struggled to do the same.

"I think he's been good. Andy has his personality, he's great. I feel like he's a guy who is on top of everything. He pays attention to every single detail and stuff like that. I really like that," Soto told SNY last weekend. "He's been open with me and talking to me about a lot of stuff."

It is not clear how much of the current Mets coaching staff will return, though Green helped assemble the revamped staff that worked with Mendoza to start the season and some of them are under contract beyond this year. Answers to those questions, and others, will come later.

For now, the Mets have certainty in the dugout entering an important offseason – one in which Bichette will be deciding whether to opt out and free agency will likely be condensed to a November frenzy ahead of the anticipated lockout in December. And that certainty comes in the form of Green, whose previous player development role means he knows better than anyone the young players who will carry the Mets' future.

title: Lady Vols basketball completes 2026-27 schedule with Coconut Hoops tournament
description: Lady Vols basketball's 2026-27 nonconference schedule is complete with two games at the Coconut Hoops tournament over Thanksgiving weekend.
fullText:
Lady Vols basketball is heading to Fort Myers, Florida, for Thanksgiving weekend this season, completing its nonconference schedule for the 2026-27 season.

Florida Gulf Coast, Creighton and Houston are also in the field for the Coconut Hoops Tournament, which will be played at Alico Arena on FGCU's campus. Tennessee will open the tournament against FGCU on Nov. 27 at 6:30 p.m. ET.

The winner of Tennessee and FGCU will face the winner of Houston and Creighton in the championship game on Nov. 29 at 6:30 p.m. The losing teams from the opening games will play at 4 p.m. on Nov. 29. Streaming information will be announced at a later date.

"We're looking forward to our trip to the Fort Myers area and to competing for the first time in Coconut Hoops," Tennessee coach Kim Caldwell said. "This multi-team event comes between a home game with UCLA and a road game at Virginia Tech, and it lines us up against some well-coached programs that have histories of success in their respective conferences. These competitive opportunities will test and prepare us for the conference schedule that lies ahead."

Tickets will go on sale Sept. 23 at 10 a.m. on the event's website.

The event, which is organized by event promotor bdG Sports, will also include Oklahoma State, Washington and UMass, which will play in a separate division. This year will be the 14th annual Coconut Hoops tournament.

title: Manchester City Are Keeping Tabs On This Gifted Midfielder: A Star In The Making?
description: On Monday’s print edition, A Bola stated that Manchester City are keeping tabs on Porto midfielder Victor Froholdt. It has been stated the Mancunian club have sent scouts to catch the Danish talent ...
fullText:
On Monday's print edition, A Bola stated that Manchester City are keeping tabs on Porto midfielder Victor Froholdt. It has been stated the Mancunian club have sent scouts to catch the Danish talent in action as they look to sign him in the future.

Froholdt has enjoyed a good run of form at the Portuguese club recently as he has produced a few impressive displays for them in the middle of the park. The 20-year-old has scored two goals in seven matches for Porto this season in all competitions.

The talented youngster is currently one of the most gifted young central midfielders in Liga Portugal. Hence, Man City would do well to get a deal done for him next year.

His current contract at the Portuguese club will expire in the summer of 2030, which could make it tough for the Mancunian club to land him on the cheap this January or at the end of this season.

PORTO, PORTUGAL – JULY 25: Victor Froholdt of FC Porto competes for the ball with Bradley Burrowes of Aston Villa during a pre-season friendly match between FC Porto and Aston Villa at Estadio do Dragao on July 25, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Octavio Passos/Getty Images)

Froholdt doesn't mind working hard for his team defensively when needed. He can even shoot the ball with power from long range and has the vision to engineer some inviting chances for his teammates to find the back of the net.

The Danish sensation is an energetic runner with the ball as well and can chip in by scoring the odd goal from midfield. However, there are some concerns over whether he can adapt to the physical side and high intensity of the Premier League if Man City manage to bring him on board next year.

Froholdt would undoubtedly improve the quality of Enzo Maresca's midfield department in the long run. He has what it takes to serve as a good rotational piece in the Mancunian club's squad.

At 20, the future looks quite promising for Froholdt as long as he continues to improve with each year. He is a star in the making, so Maresca would be wise to step up his efforts to land him in 2027. However, Man City would have to be patient with his development before they can get the best out of him.

title: ESPN analyst believes Buccaneers might already regret Baker Mayfield's extension
description: It's been a rough first two weeks for Mayfield on his new deal.
fullText:
ESPN analyst believes Buccaneers might already regret Baker Mayfield's extension originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Coming into the 2026 season, Baker Mayfield made his displeasure about not having a new contract well known. But the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, just as they did with Vita Vea, gave Mayfield a new contract extension.

Shortly before the season began, the Buccaneers signed Mayfield to a new three-year, $165 million contract extension. It was a solid payday and security for Mayfield, but for the Buccaneers, it might've been a mistake.

ESPN's Ben Solak thinks that the Buccaneers might already regret signing that extension with Mayfield after the team's 0-2 start and Week 2 loss to the Cleveland Browns. While harsh, the extension does take on a new light with this start to the season.

"I think ... the Buccaneers are already regretting that Baker Mayfield deal," Solak writes. "Mayfield has not played well through the first two games of the season."

The Buccaneers are 0-2, with losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and the Browns. Mayfield has not been great, throwing for 398 yards but only one touchdown. He also has one interception, and his 45.4 QBR is not a good mark at all, ranking 27th in the NFL.

Mayfield's struggles early this season in the team's 0-2 start might already have the Buccaneers regretting the $165 million deal they handed Mayfield this offseason.

While there's still plenty of time for Mayfield to make good on that deal, the questions about his game following a brutal Week 2 loss to the Browns of all teams aren't going to help his case.

MORE: Todd Monken hits back at Mike Tomlin after first win as Browns coach: 'F— that'

One of the biggest points Solak makes in his belief that the Buccaneers might regret this extension isn't about the deal for Mayfield itself, but rather doing it before this season.

Had the Buccaneers waited until after the 2026 season to see how Mayfield performed, it likely wouldn't have cost them much more than the $55 million they're spending on him now, even if he played well.

A deal in the $60 million range per-year over three years would be a lot, but it would be worth it if Mayfield put together a strong 2026 season. But if he struggled, like he has thus far, then something closer to $50 million per-year would've made sense.

Solak believes the Buccaneers might already start to regret their Mayfield deal. It's not a failure just yet, as it's two games into his new deal. But so far, the signs are not good, and this deal might end up being a big mistake.

title: Yankees must start Carlos Rodón in potential Wild Card Game 3 against Red Sox
description: New York Yankees left-hander Carlos Rodón has been pitching well as the season winds down.
fullText:
The 2026 MLB season concludes on Sunday, with all 30 teams beginning play around 3 p.m. ET. The New York Yankees are one of six clubs to officially punch their ticket to the postseason so far and are 90-66 on the year.

The Yankees' superstar outfielder Aaron Judge only managed to appear in 66 games this season due first to a broken rib and now to a strained right calf. Even with Judge missing all the time he did, New York still won a good bit without him.

The problem is that they did not win quite enough, and will likely have to play in the Wild Card round as a result. The team is second place in the American League East, five games behind the Tampa Bay Rays with six to play (three against them).

The Yankees just concluded game one of four versus the Rays Tuesday afternoon in the first game of a split doubleheader. They won 2-0 on the back of eight shutout innings from lefty starter Carlos Rodón (7-3, 2.67 ERA).

MORE: Cam Schlittler draws comparison to Dodgers legend ahead of Yankees postseason

Aug 29, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees starting pitcher Carlos Rodon (55) pitches against the Boston Red Sox during the first inning at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

There are still many possibilities, but in all likelihood the Yankees will host a best-of-three in the Wild Card versus their rival Boston Red Sox next week. Both teams are fairly locked into their seedings for the moment.

Games 1 & 2 should belong to right-handed AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler and elite lefty Max Fried. That leaves a starting pitcher decision for the Yankees to make regarding a possible winner-take-all Game 3.

They could have right-hander Gerrit Cole (9-9, 3.63 ERA) take the mound, as he has been mostly good following his return from Tommy John Surgery in late May. However, the hot hand lately has been their No. 4 starter in the aforementioned Rodón.

An interesting report from The Athletic's Chris Kirschner came out after game one of the Rays series. Manager Aaron Boone said that Tuesday was "potentially" Rodón's last regular season start.

The Yankees are still in play to catch the Rays in the AL East, but it is incredibly unlikely they do so. First, they would have to sweep this four-game series against them, then hope the Rays crumble in their final series of the year at the Philadelphia Phillies, all while themselves sweeping the Baltimore Orioles at home.

If Tampa Bay wins just one of these games in the Bronx, they will take the division and the AL's No. 1 seed. Boone saying "potentially" probably meant that Rodón could start Sunday versus Baltimore if the team is still alive in the division race.

Seeing as they likely will not be, that would open the door for Rodón to pitch a Game 3 versus the Red Sox. Cole has famously struggled against them in his Yankee career, and Rodón has been on fire lately.

title: Sixers guard VJ Edgecombe ranked No. 72 player in the league for 2027
description: Philadelphia 76ers guard VJ Edgecombe comes in ranked as the No. 72 player in the league heading into the 2026-27 season.
fullText:
VJ Edgecombe had one helluva maiden season in the NBA. The No. 3 pick of the 2025 draft averaged 16.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 4.2 assists along with 1.4 steals per game. He helped the Philadelphia 76ers on both ends of the floor and took games over in the clutch as well.

Edgecombe had an up-and-down postseason, but he did score 30 points with 10 rebounds in a Game 2 win over the Boston Celtics. He was the first rookie to have 30 and 10 in a game since the great Tim Duncan back in 1998. It's obvious that Edgecombe is headed for stardom in the league.

ESPN ranked the top 100 players in the NBA heading into the 2026-27 season and Edgecombe comes in ranked No. 72:

It might seem natural that the No. 3 pick in the 2025 draft would finish third in Rookie of the Year voting, but that placement undersells Edgecombe's impressive debut season. As a Day 1 starter for a team that reached the second round of the playoffs, Edgecombe averaged 16.0 points, 5.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists while making 35% of his 3s. Perhaps most impressively, he ranked 11th in the league in minutes despite having to adjust to a full NBA schedule.

If there is one blemish on Edgecombe's resume right now, it's the poor 3-point shooting in the playoffs as it dropped from 35.4% in the regular season to 29.2% in the playoffs. As he heads into his second season in the league, Edgecombe will look to help the Sixers reach the mountaintop. Expectations have risen when considering the team added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James in an effort to get the job done.

title: Jaguars announce addition at tight end heading into Week 3
description: The Jacksonville Jaguars announced a tight end addition to the practice squad on Tuesday.
fullText:
The Jacksonville Jaguars announced an addition to the practice squad on Tuesday, signing tight end Brenden Bates.

Bates went undrafted in 2024 out of Kentucky and originally signed with the Chicago Bears. Since then, he has spent time with Houston, Cleveland, and the New York Jets.

Over the last two seasons, Bates has appeared in nine games on offense, playing 179 total snaps. He has four receptions for 48 yards with 85% of his snaps coming as a blocker, according to PFF. Bates has played 86 career special teams snaps as well during that span.

Bates, 26, appeared in 57 games while at Kentucky. The Jaguars team site notes that while in college, Bates spent time with Liam Coen, Chris Rodriguez, and Josh Hines-Allen at various points.

On the active roster, Brenton Strange, Nate Boerkircher, Quintin Morris, and Tanner Koziol make up the tight end room. Bates joins Hayden Rucci as the second tight end on the practice squad.

title: Jedd Fisch vs. P.J. Fleck: Who’s under more pressure in this week's Big Ten opener?
description: Saturday night's game feels like it could be a swinging-doors moment on both teams' 2026 seasons.
fullText:
Washington opened this season at No. 17 in the preseason Associated Press (AP) top 25 poll. Despite starting the season 3-0, they've since completely fallen out of the poll, and the Huskies have a lot to prove in this week's Big Ten opener against the Gophers.

The Huskies played in the 2023 National Championship game under former head coach Kaelen DeBoer, which was the final year of the four-team College Football Player era. Jedd Fisch was hired as DeBoer's replacement that offseason. He went 6-7 in 2024, 9-4 last season, and this year feels like a key point of his Washington tenure.

"Jedd Fisch has done a really good job; I've known him for a very long time. Heather and his wife are friends. Just a ton of respect for what he does and how he does it. He's a great playcaller, an offensive mind. Coach Walters on the other side; he was the head coach at Purdue, coordinator at Illinois. So we have a lot of familiarity with him," Gophers head coach P.J. Fleck said on his weekly radio show on Tuesday.

Despite the Huskies' undefeated record, many experts are doubting whether or not they'll come anywhere close to their preseason expectations. Star quarterback Demond Williams has accounted for 79.7% of their total offense through three games, masking some issues that could come up against better competition.

Washington's nonconference schedule ranked as the third easiest in all of FBS football. Wins of 14 points, two points and 32 points at home over Washington State, Utah State and Eastern Washington didn't exactly instil confidence that Fisch's program is ready to take the next step as a legit College Football Playoff contender.

"They got a really good football team, man, and I'll tell you what, they've done a really good job building their roster. I know they've got a few injuries here and there. I think everybody does in the country. We do too. At the end of the day, we gotta go out and play our best football; we really do," Fleck continued

The current betting odds have Washington favored by around 10 points, which means that the experts expect the Huskies to roll. But the Gophers already have a loss under their belts, and they have a rivalry game for the Little Brown Jug looming in Week 5 against Michigan. A loss would extend their road losing streak to six games, and it would put them in a big 2-2 hole to start 2026.

Minnesota and Washington are two states with more similarities than you think, but their football programs are currently in two very different spots. Both head coaches should face plenty of pressure heading into Saturday's game, but for very different reasons.

We are in the age of big media consolidation and content networks. But even with the proliferation of AI, nothing can beat the quality and inherent knowledge of local sports journalism. Our writing room consists of a Wildcat, a Gopher, and even a Mustang. We know the Minnesota towns and the great names that played on its diamonds, courts, fields or rinks. We would appreciate your readership and support!

title: GB boxers guaranteed three medals at Europeans
description: Britain guarantee at least three medals at the European Boxing Championships in Bulgaria as Chantelle Reid, Damar Thomas and Abdul Burton all reach the semi-finals.
fullText:
Great Britain are guaranteed at least three medals at the European Boxing Championships in Bulgaria after Chantelle Reid, Damar Thomas and Abdul Burton reached the semi-finals.

Reid cruised to a 5-0 win over Ireland's Evelyn Igharo in a women's light-middleweight contest at the Asics Arena Sports Hall in Sofia.

The 28-year-old Commonwealth Games silver medallist will face Serbia's Milena Matovic in the last four on Wednesday.

Thomas won by the same margin in a men's super-heavyweight fight against Georgia's Nikoloz Begadze and the 21-year-old will take on Mahammad Abdullayev of Azerbaijan in the semi-finals.

Burton, 20, beat home favourite and Olympic bronze medallist Javier Ibanez 3-2 to secure a meeting with Turkey's Semih Gumus.

"Sometimes you have got to dig in and when things went against me I had to get stuck in and show who I was," Burton said.

"I am young, hungry and here to take over."

Lauren Mackie, Amy Broadhurst, Callum Makin and Oladimeji Shittu are all due in quarter-final action on Wednesday, but over half of Britain's squad of 15 are now out.

On Tuesday, flyweight Ruby White was beaten 3-2 by Olympic silver medal winner Hatice Akbas of Turkey while Emily Asquith suffered a 5-0 defeat in her light-heavyweight bout with Ireland's Lisa O'Rourke.

In the men's heavyweight division, Commonwealth Games champion Isaac Okoh bowed out with a 3-0 defeat by Germany's Kevin Lebowski.

title: Steelers Sign Former Giants Wide Receiver
description: The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed wide receiver Isaiah Hodgins to their practice squad, the team announced on Tuesday. The Giants […]
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed wide receiver Isaiah Hodgins to their practice squad, the team announced on Tuesday. The Giants signed Hodgins off the Steelers' practice squad last November. He re-signed with the club in March.

Hodgins was part of the Giants' final roster cuts late last month.

Hodgins, 27, joined the Steelers practice squad on Sep. 16 as the team continued to search for wide receiver talent. However, he was never able to establish himself in Pittsburgh and now reunites with the Giants.

The 6-foot-4, 200-pound receiver was a sixth-round draft pick in the 2020 NFL Draft by the Buffalo Bills, who he spent the first three years (2020-22) of his professional career with. After missing his entire rookie season with a pair of injuries, he spent most of 2021 on the practice squad, appearing in just one game.

In 2022, he again started on the practice squad, but was promoted to the active roster on Oct. 8 and played against the Steelers the next day, making four catches for 41 yards.

After playing in two games, he was placed on waivers and claimed by New York, where he appeared in eight more games and made five starts.

Hodgins' best career game came that Dec. 24 for the Giants against the Miami Dolphins, when he caught eight passes for 89 yards and a touchdown.

He finished the 2022 season with 10 games played, five starts, and 37 catches for 392 yards and four touchdowns. He re-signed with the Giants for the 2023 season, and played in all 17 games, making nine starts and catching 21 passes for 230 yards and three scores.

Hodgins again spent the 2024 season on the Giants' practice squad without appearing in a game. This offseason, he signed with the San Francisco 49ers but was waived during final roster cuts in August. He had four catches for 36 yards this preseason.

Hodgins posted a 4.61-second 40-yard dash coming out of Oregon State in 2020. He also had a 36.5-inch vertical jump and a 10-foot-4 broad jump.

He played three seasons with the Beavers, all as a starter. His best year was in 2019, when he caught 86 passes for 1,171 yards and 13 touchdowns.

title: O'Neill receives Celtic backing after 'painful' week
description: Celtic will "come together and support" manager Martin O'Neill after a "painful" week for the club, says chief executive Michael Nicholson.
fullText:
Celtic will "come together and support" manager Martin O'Neill after a "painful" week for the club, chief executive Michael Nicholson has said.

O'Neill had indicated that he would use the international break to consider his future following two defeats to Rangers, either side of a home loss to Ferencvaros in the Europa League.

In the wake of Sunday's 1-0 derby defeat at Celtic Park, 74-year-old O'Neill had said "it might be time to wrap it up".

However, Nicholson suggested the club will rally round the manager who has delivered nine trophies over two spells.

His remarks came with the latest financial figures revealing a drop of nearly £33m in revenue.

A loss of £4.8m is largely down to the failure to reach last year's Champions League and Celtic have missed out again, squandering a 4-0 aggregate lead in their play-off with LASK last month.

"Having started well in the Premiership this season, we experienced disappointment in the Champions League play-off," said Nicholson in a written statement accompanying the financial results.

"Reaching the league phase of the Champions League is an objective for us all, and we are sorry not to have achieved it.

"On top of that, the losses in the last week have been painful for us all. We will now come together and support Martin and the players, as we focus our efforts on achieving success domestically and in the Europa League."

title: Legendary Celtics Coach Makes Jump to Broadcasting Ahead of 2026-27 Season
description: The Hall of Fame coach is swapping the sideline for the broadcast booth.
fullText:
Legendary Celtics Coach Makes Jump to Broadcasting Ahead of 2026-27 Season originally appeared on NESN. 

Doc Rivers is returning to the broadcast booth.

NBC Sports announced Monday that the Naismith Basketball Hall of Famer will join its NBA coverage as a game analyst for the 2026-27 season. Rivers will work games across NBC, Peacock and NBCSN as the network begins its new NBA coverage next month.

Rivers brings more than 40 years of NBA experience to the role as both a player and coach. He spent 12 seasons in the NBA as a point guard, including a stint with the Atlanta Hawks that earned him an All-Star selection in 1988.

His coaching career included stops with the Orlando Magic, Boston Celtics, Los Angeles Clippers, Philadelphia 76ers and Milwaukee Bucks. Rivers' most notable run came in Boston, where he coached the Celtics to the 2008 NBA championship and another NBA Finals appearance in 2010.

Rivers finished his coaching career with 1,194 wins, the sixth-most in NBA history. He was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame as part of the 2026 class.

The move also marks a return to NBC for Rivers. He previously worked as a studio analyst for the network during the 2012 London Olympics according to an ESPN release.

Rivers said he is now fully retired from coaching and plans to give broadcasting his full attention.

"I loved playing the game, I loved coaching it, and I've always loved talking about it," Rivers said, per NBC Sports. "I'm excited to be back and share my perspective alongside such a talented team."

Rivers also will have a familiar face on the NBC Sports team. His son, Austin Rivers, is an NBA veteran and analyst for the network. Doc Rivers coached Austin with the Clippers from 2015-18, making them the first father-son duo in NBA history to work together as coach and player.

Doc Rivers will join his son, Austin, at NBC Sports as a game analyst for this upcoming NBA season ❤️🏀 pic.twitter.com/q40E0f9OJr

Several other NBC analysts also have ties to Rivers. He coached Grant Hill and Tracy McGrady with the Magic, Brian Scalabrine with the Celtics and Jamal Crawford with the Clippers.

After spending years on the sidelines, Rivers will now offer his perspective from the other side of the game as NBC launches its latest chapter of NBA coverage.

title: Colts place DE Micheal Clemons on IR, confirm signing WR Darius Slayton
description: After logging just 38 snaps in his first 2 games as a Colt, DE Micheal Clemons has been placed on injured reserve and will miss at least four games
fullText:
The Colts have placed edge rusher Micheal Clemons on injured reserve, the team announced Tuesday. The move sidelines Clemons, the 29-year-old who inked a three-year deal worth up to $18.5 million with Indianapolis in free agency, for at least the next four games through the team's Week 6 home game against the Titans.

Clemons, one of two notable defensive line additions the Colts made in free agency in March after missing out on now-Ravens star Trey Hendrickson, has played just 38 total defensive snaps in his first two games in Indianapolis (25.7%) as consistently the second defensive end off the bench behind second-year second-round pick Jaylahn Tuimoloau.

He played 24 snaps (30%) on defense in the team's 33-30 overtime loss Sunday night to the Chiefs in Kansas City and two on special teams. The team did not announce Clemons' specific ailment with the news, but Clemons briefly left Sunday night's game in the first half with a toe injury, though he did return. Through two games in Indianapolis, Clemons has not recorded a stat.

The move clears a roster spot for free agent wide receiver signing Darius Slayton, who the Colts landed this week after appearing to lose top receiving option Alec Pierce for a substantial amount of time with a reaggravation of his heel injury he had surgery on in March.

The Colts also announced the release of running back Anderson Castle from the practice squad Tuesday but have not yet provided a formal update on Pierce's status moving forward after the fifth-year receiver left Sunday night's game in the first quarter on a cart after hopping off the field on one foot in serious pain. X-rays on Pierce's left heel were negative, but a league source told IndyStar Monday night the receiver is likely to miss several weeks in an attempt to rehab his injury in-season and avoid surgery that could end his 2026 campaign.

Joel A. Erickson and Nathan Brown cover the Colts all season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Colts Insider newsletter.

title: 3 potential Detroit Lions trade targets to boost struggling secondary

Detroit still has postseason aspirations, so waiting for the secondary to get healthy could be a risky play given how competitive the NFC North is this season. Adding another capable defensive back would provide immediate relief, while adding depth until Branch and Joseph return.

title: Can the Packers survive Zach Bako-Bewele's season-ending injury?
description: Green Bay is now relying on Anthony Belton making rapid progress if they are to survive Zach Bako-Bewele's devastating injury.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers got the news they were dreading regarding Zach Bako-Bewele's injury, as it has been confirmed the right tackle has a torn patellar injury which will knock him out for the year.

Bako-Bewele suffered the injury on the Packers' third offensive play against the Jets, and it is the same patellar which he partially tore near the end of last season. It is a devastating blow for a Green Bay offensive line that already looked shaky and will now be without its best player for the remainder of the season. The question now is whether they have any hope of surviving without ZBB.

If that is to happen, Anthony Belton will have to step up and play up to his draft pedigree first and foremost.

The 2025 second-round pick practiced almost exclusively at tackle during the summer, and while that decision was questioned at the time – as he was presumed to be in the competition to start at right guard despite not practicing there – it now looks like a wise decision by the Packers.

They needed to know who the backup tackle was, and Belton's profile most leant itself to the position among Green Bay's options. He has the size at 6-6 and 336 pounds and was a left tackle in college.

Belton played just 86 snaps at tackle as a rookie, before 56 on Sunday after stepping in for Bako-Bewele. The Packers will be hoping his experience during training camp will stand him in good stead to take over at right tackle. They are relying on him to rise to the challenge.

In the three games he has played there, Belton had a 66.6 pass block grade against the Commanders last year, 39.2 versus the Browns and 60.5 against the Jets on Sunday, when he allowed only three quarterback hurries in pass protection, but did commit two penalties.

The injury to Bako-Bewele also has a knock-on effect as there is less depth across the entire line. In a best-case scenario health-wise, the Packers will now have a starting five of Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Belton.

With ZBB out, none of their offensive lineman have a PFF grade higher than 58.2 through two games (60 is average).

The top options from the bench will be Jager Burton, Donovan Jennings and John Williams. There are more injuries though, as Banks and Jennings were both estimated to be DNPs on Monday's injury report with knee/toe injuries for the former and a hand issue for the latter.

If Banks and Jennings cannot go on Thursday against Atlanta, Burton would presumably step in at left guard. Frankly, it is hard to imagine the Packers cobbling together an offensive line capable of going on a run to the Super Bowl, which is the team's expectation.

That is dependent on some significant development from a group of mostly young linemen, and an impressive coaching job to not only eradicate the mental errors that have plagued them early on, but also come up with effective plans to protect (or hide) the weaknesses of the O-line.

It is hard to know whether O-line coach Luke Butkus is doing as little to improve the situation as the outside seems to have decided, but if they are to salvage the situation, it is going to take a huge effort from players and coaches alike, and right now, there is not much reason for optimism.

title: Mets remove interim tag, make Andy Green full-time manager with 3-year deal
description: Green took over on June 26 after the firing of Carlos Mendoza.
fullText:
The New York Mets have signed interim manager Andy Green to a three-year deal, the team announced on Tuesday.

"Andy has connected with and pushed our players to perform, despite the disappointment of the season," Mets owners Steve and Alex Cohen said in a statement. "Over the last several months he has brought discipline, accountability and positivity to the clubhouse, attributes we were seeking in our next manager."

The 49-year-old Green took over for Carlos Mendoza, who was fired on June 26 after a 34-47 start to the 2026 season. He was originally hired by the Mets in 2023 in a player development role. He previously managed the San Diego Padres to a 274-366 record between 2016 and 2019.

After being handed the interim role, president of baseball operations David Stearns said that Green would move back to the front office after the season. That plan has changed over the past three months.

"When I accepted the interim role, I didn't anticipate it becoming permanent, but the more time I spent with our players and staff, the clearer it became that this is where my passion and experience could make the greatest impact," Green said in a statement.

Through 75 games under Green, the Mets have posted a 37-38 record and are 31-28 since the All-Star break.

With six games left in the regular season, New York is last in the NL East with a 71-85 record. They will miss out on the postseason for the second consecutive season and third in the last four.

title: Red Sox Get Encouraging Signs From Two Injured Stars Ahead of Postseason
description: Both Garrett Crochet and Curtis Mead appeared to take steps toward potential returns on Tuesday.
fullText:
Red Sox Get Encouraging Signs From Two Injured Stars Ahead of Postseason originally appeared on NESN. 

Could the Red Sox get some reinforcements ahead of the postseason?

While there's still work to do for Boston, looking to secure a top-two wild card spot in the American League over the next few days, the team can also officially start planning for the playoffs.

For the most part, the Red Sox know who their key contributors will be in the AL Wild Card round. But on Tuesday, fans got positive updates on two injured stars, both of whom appear to be nearing potential returns.

Here's the latest on both Garrett Crochet and Curtis Mead as they work toward getting back to full health for the Red Sox.

Boston's pitching staff has been terrific in 2026 despite the absence of Crochet, who has been out since April with a lat strain and other shoulder inflammation. But ahead of the postseason, it appears Crochet is ramping up at a perfect time.

Crochet throwing live BP with Ceddanne at Fenway today 👀 pic.twitter.com/Iwv2R14iVk

On Tuesday, Crochet was seen completing a live BP session against Ceddanne Rafaela, throwing 16 pitches that included a velocity in the 94-96 mph range, according to Tyler Milliken.

Garrett Crochet ended up throwing a total of 16 pitches in his first live BP.

Velocity was in the 94-96 range. Few ticks up from the last time he threw a regular bullpen. Currently feeling good and thinks he can get outs.

Some great video from @alexspeier. pic.twitter.com/ZMsMmUXzvU

Notably, per Chris Cotillo, Crochet also told reporters that he thinks he could "get outs" with the way his live session went.

On Saturday, new full-time manager Chad Tracy also provided the latest on Crochet and whether he could return, potentially as a reliever for the postseason.

"I think it just depends on how he feels coming out of it, how much volume we give him," Tracy said, per MLB.com. "So it's hard to say. I know it's not a great answer, but it's just really how it is. How does he feel after each step? So when he does that, how does he feel? And then determine from there. Do we give him more hitters or do we want to put him in a game? It's hard to say until you know how he feels.

Meanwhile, infielder Curtis Mead, who was injured in his Red Sox debut in July, also appeared to take a step forward on Tuesday. According to Cotillo, Mead, at one point during Crochet's session, appeared to be getting ready to step into the batter's box as well. Over the weekend, Mead began hitting off a tee and playing catch, per MLB.com.

There's no guarantee that Crochet or Mead will be ready in time for a likely best-of-three playoff series, but either could provide Boston with a huge boost. At their best, Crochet is one of baseball's best left-handed pitchers, while Mead hit 17 home runs before joining the Red Sox this season.

title: Barcelona set to leave the Camp Nou again

fullText:
La Liga champions Barcelona have put in place plans to depart the club's beloved Spotify Camp Nou ground for the latest time next year.

These plans were recently made public by Blaugrana treasurer and economic vice-president Ferran Olive.

Barcelona are of course not long back at the Camp Nou. After initially closing their stadium for long overdue renovations in the summer of 2023, the Catalans pencilled in a return date late in 2024.

This comeback was ultimately pushed all the way to November of last year, however, as a result of a string of unforeseen delays.

And as alluded to above, in the not-so-distant future, all of a Barca persuasion will be forced to bid temporary farewell to the Camp Nou once again. As per a report from The Athletic:

'To fit the roof and finish the stadium completely, the team will need to leave. Design plans mean the roof has to be built from inside the stadium, requiring building materials to be stationed where the Camp Nou pitch is.'

For this reason, Ferran Olive has announced plans for Hansi Flick and his squad to leave their ground behind for the first half of next season, with a view to returning in January of 2028.

title: Arizona State men's golf hires former PGA Tour winner as assistant coach
description: The Arizona State men's golf program announced Tuesday it hired James Hahn as a full-time assistant coach.
fullText:
The Arizona State men's golf program announced Tuesday that it hired James Hahn as a full-time assistant coach.

Hahn, who played collegiately at California from 2000-02, won twice on the PGA Tour, making 291 career starts and nearly $13 million in career earnings.

"I'm incredibly excited to join the Sun Devil men's golf program and be part of one of the elite powerhouses in collegiate golf," Hahn said in a release. "I'm honored to share the knowledge and experiences I've gained throughout my professional golf career to help elevate the process and further the development of our players. I am here to support the team and each player in any way I can, both on and off the golf course. I'm grateful for the opportunity and can't wait to get started and contribute to the continued success of Sun Devil Golf."

Hahn replaces Thomas Sutton, who left coach Matt Thurmond's staff this summer to take the head coaching position at Washington.

"James is a world-class golfer and person and I'm really excited to work alongside him," Thurmond said. "He brings the most relevant of experience and I can see our player development surging with his coaching. He's has been where these guys want to go and he's an excellent teacher, coach, and mentor. We are getting better today. I'm definitely going to want James to play and practice with the team as much as possible. Maybe even have him coach the boys on his dance moves."

Arizona State won the Fighting Illini Invitational this past weekend at Olympia Fields after opening the season with a T-6 finish at Sahalee.

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

title: More support for Bayern Munich star Harry Kane to win Ballon d’Or
description: The FC Bayern star has backers.
fullText:
Vladimír Šmicer has thrown his support behind Harry Kane in the Ballon d'Or race, arguing that the Bayern Munich striker deserves to be considered the favorite despite competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé.

Šmicer, the former Czech Republic international and Liverpool midfielder who famously scored in the 2005 Champions League final against AC Milan, believes Kane's overall body of work makes him the most deserving candidate. He also pointed to Kane's success in Germany and his continued excellence after leaving England.

"The Ballon d'Or is very open this year but I think Harry Kane should be the big favourite. Lamine Yamal will be there as well but he didn't have a great World Cup. He was just very good for Barcelona but he's been injured. A lot could depend on who is the best player in the next few months," Smicer told Grosvenor Sport. "Kylian Mbappe is another favourite as well because he had a very good World Cup but he was average for Real Madrid in the first half of the year so I think, for all that he has done in his career, it should be Harry Kane.

"I would like to see him win the Ballon d'Or to go with his Golden Boot and the Bundesliga because why not? He's been brilliant in Germany, and he was brilliant in England before that as well."

The argument reflects a broader discussion surrounding this year's award. Kane has already received significant backing from figures around Bayern Munich, while other contenders such as Yamal and Mbappé have their own cases based on their club and international performances.

For Kane, however, the prize would represent something more than another individual honor. After years of elite production without winning the Ballon d'Or, lifting the trophy would add another major individual achievement to a career that has already included the Golden Boot and Bundesliga title.
